messages:
ryan: Customer (acme-inc) hit a major regression: structured JSON responses intermittently contain fields from a previous request — basically two different JSON objects glued together. They reported 8% of calls failing parsing.

maria: Thanks — any request IDs or example responses? Do we have their region and model pinned?

ryan: Request id: r-0b72f9a3, region: us-west-2, model: open-7b-redwood-v2, mode: json. Attached example: 

ashley: Paste the exact response if you can. Also, did they upgrade tokens or rotate keys recently?

ryan: Example response (customer's parser threw a JSONDecodeError):

```
{"order_id": "A123", "status": "confirmed", "items": [{"sku": "X1", "qty": 1}], "meta": {"user": "u-55"}}
{"order_id": "B987", "status": "pending", "items": [{"sku": "Y2", "qty": 2}], "meta": {"user": "u-78"}}
```

ryan: Note: that's two objects concatenated with no array wrapper. Customer expects a single object per request but sometimes gets the previous response prefixed.

kevin: That pattern screams caching/batching window crosswrite. Any correlation with high QPS bursts or batching enabled?

ryan: They run steady ~150 req/s, occasional spikes to 600. Using JSON mode with kvcache enabled (default). They said issues started after we rolled out batching window tuning (last Wednesday).

maria: Can you repro locally with their prompt? Also include the raw response body and the x-request-id / x-host-ts from the API headers.

ryan: Repro steps I ran:
```
# single threaded loop hitting their payload
for i in range(1,400):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"open-7b-redwood-v2","json_schema": {"type":"object"},"input":"<customer-prompt>","stream":false}' \
  | jq -R -c . # capture raw
```
I saw the concatenated objects after a tight burst (around iteration 172). Headers: x-request-id: r-0b72f9a3, x-runtime-node: node-14, x-batch-window: 20ms

ashley: Can you grab engine logs around node-14 for that timeframe? Look for messages: `kvcache: flush` `batch: assign` `batch: commit` and any errors about async prefetch.

ryan: Attached snippet from node-14 logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.123Z] batch: assign id=bd-44 window=20ms size=12
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.143Z] kvcache: serve id=bd-44 session=se-993
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.143Z] kvcache: prefetch id=bd-43 -> id=bd-44 (race)
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.146Z] kvcache: flush id=bd-44 writes=1
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.146Z] response: stream end id=bd-44 req=r-0b72f9a3
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.146Z] response: stream start id=bd-45 req=r-0b72f9b7
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.147Z] kvcache: write id=bd-44 buffer_len=512
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.147Z] kvcache: write id=bd-45 buffer_len=1024
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.148Z] http: out id=bd-44 body_len=1024
[2026-03-16T14:22:51.148Z] http: out id=bd-45 body_len=1536
```

maria: That `prefetch id=bd-43 -> id=bd-44 (race)` line looks concerning. Could be a window where kvcache writes overlapped and ordering isn't locked per request.

ashley: We should try forcing single-threaded batches (batch-window=0) to confirm. If it disappears, it's batching race. Also check whether `response: stream end` / `response: stream start` events can interleave buffers — maybe stream boundaries aren't flushing buffer boundaries to HTTP layer correctly.

ryan: Customer also says some calls were billed even when parsing failed and they aborted. They put a pause on usage pending fix — billing impact reported. Can finance or billing flag those invoices?

kevin: Filing a billing exception ticket now (TKT-5892). We'll need to include sample request ids and timestamps.

eng-runtime-bot: @channel Auto-alert created: ISSUE-RT-1122 (probable kvcache write race in batch-window path). Linked to owner: eng-runtime. Priority: P1 if customer impact >5% errors.

maria: Next actions: (1) Ashley to reproduce with internal stress tool and run with batch-window variants (0ms, 10ms, 50ms). (2) Ryan to collect the full raw response bodies + headers for 10 examples. (3) Kevin to submit billing exception and notify account exec. (4) If reproed, escalate to eng-runtime for a hotfix to kvcache flush ordering.

ashley: I'm starting the local stress run now. Initial plan: toggle `BATCH_WINDOW_MS` and `KVCACHE_PREFETCH=true/false`, capture http body lengths and verify boundary markers. Will report results within 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ryan: Thanks — I'll keep the customer updated and ask for their ephemeral logs and 10 failing request ids.

maria: Also add a temporary mitigation in docs: recommend `batch_window_ms=0` or `disable_kvcache_prefetch=true` for affected customers until we push a fix. Put that in a private KB so support can triage quickly.

kevin: Billing ticket created and AE looped in.

eng-runtime-bot: @eng-runtime assigned ISSUE-RT-1122 to ashley. Deadline: 48h.

maria: Good. Keep updates in this thread. If anyone sees other affected customers, DM me so we can aggregate traces. :white_check_mark:
